reviews.reason: The judgment applies Article 67 of Regulation 883/2004 and Article 60(1) of Regulation 987/2009 to the parent actually living with the children in Spain. Sections 62–64 EStG and Article 1(i)(1)(i) determine entitlement and participants, including unmarried or formerly married parents; the Article 1(i)(2) fallback does not control. Article 60 applies through Article 67 regardless of whether an Article 68 conflict also exists. Other national entitlement conditions remain necessary. The fiction relocates actual family residence and does not create a common household. The German father’s application is considered for the priority mother and does not transfer entitlement because she did not apply. The historical monthly amounts are case facts, not current parameters. This remains bearing and unencoded. Exact BStBl II membership is not independently established by this review.

Although the operative order lifts a procedural stay, its reasons determine the application of EStG 62(1) versus 62(2): missing employment permission under historical SGB III 284 alone does not remove an EU national’s free-movement status. Paragraphs 13–17 require the competent immigration authority’s formal determination under FreizügG/EU 5 and 6 before the described transition to AufenthG, preserving the distinction between worker access restrictions and citizenship-based movement. This is not a universal entitlement independent of remaining national conditions, nor an authority for Familienkassen to make that loss determination themselves. The historical Polish transitional regime is not a current transition parameter; paragraph 11 itself contains both 30 November and 30 April 2011, so no endpoint is silently chosen from this text. The substantive free-movement dependency remains bearing and unencoded despite the procedural disposition. Exact BStBl II membership is not independently established by this review.

reviews.reason: This instrument suspends the pending revision and asks three preliminary questions about the whole-family fiction, the distinction between substantive entitlement and application, and a conditional waiting period. Its competing interpretations, reported lower-court reasoning and party submissions are not an operative final rule awarding entitlement. The subsequent CJEU C-378/14 judgment resolves the first two questions and declines to answer the third; BFH III R17/13 of 4 February 2016 applies that answer. Those distinct final instruments remain bearing and unencoded in this ledger. No additional current computable Kindergeld rule is supplied by the reference order beyond statutory restatement and questions resolved by those retained instruments; in particular the four-year limitation discussion is not an enacted waiting period or transfer rule. Exclusion is confined to this preliminary-reference identity, not its final judgments. Exact BStBl II membership is not independently established by this review.

reviews.paragraphs_reviewed: complete German judgment; paragraphs 26–52 and both operative holdings
reviews.reason: Articles 67 of Regulation 883/2004 and 60(1) of Regulation 987/2009 require consideration of the whole family as residing under the competent state’s legislation. Article 1(i)(1)(i) refers participants to national entitlement rules, including separated or divorced parents. The competent national institution determines entitlement after all remaining national conditions are met. Article 68 priority does not apply where the other state provides no entitlement, while Article 60 can still apply through Article 67. Considering another parent’s application does not transfer substantive entitlement merely because the foreign-resident priority parent did not apply. Paragraph 51 declines the third question after the negative answer to the second; no waiting period is prescribed. Both operative holdings remain bearing and unencoded. It is not a universal foreign-parent award or an independent current rate rule. Exact BStBl II membership is not independently established by this review.
